recent_posts.title: New in Livebook Teams: Google Workspace integration, App folders, and more
recent_posts.summary: Livebook Teams v0.18 introduces Google Workspace SSO integration for access control, a redesigned apps page with folder organization and search capabilities, folder-based access permissions, direct Git repository notebook access, and comprehensive audit logging documentation. These features help teams manage authentication, organize internal tools, control access at granular levels, and maintain production accountability through detailed audit trails.

recent_posts.title: Code navigation with go to definition of modules and functions
recent_posts.summary: Livebook v0.14 introduces features to simplify code navigation. The Outline panel now lists module definitions, helping users jump directly to them. Additionally, users can quickly navigate to function definitions by holding Command (on macOS) or Ctrl (on Windows/Linux) and clicking. These updates aim to enhance the developer experience.

recent_posts.title: Livebook 0.13: expose an HTTP API from your notebook
recent_posts.summary: Livebook 0.13 introduces Kino.Proxy, a feature allowing you to expose API endpoints directly from your notebook or Livebook app. This enhancement leverages the Plug library for handling HTTP requests and can handle external triggers, such as GitHub webhooks. The post includes examples and showcases potential use cases, like building APIs to automate processes.

recent_posts.title: Welcoming Tigris as a new sponsor of Livebook!
recent_posts.summary: Tigris is announced as the latest Livebook sponsor, providing a globally distributed S3-compatible object storage service with low latency. Tigris offers intuitive usage similar to AWS S3 and allows for easy transitioning of code. It automatically caches objects in the region closest to the request's origin, improving subsequent access times. Tigris combines object storage with CDN capabilities, resulting in a great user experience and developer experience.

recent_posts.title: Vim and Emacs key bindings
recent_posts.summary: Livebook now supports Vim and Emacs key bindings for a more pleasant and productive coding experience. Install the latest version of Livebook to start using this feature.

recent_posts.title: Integration with SnowFlake and Microsoft SQL Server
recent_posts.summary: Livebook now has built-in integrations for Snowflake and Microsoft SQL Server, allowing users to easily connect, execute queries, and load results into an Explorer dataframe. The Snowflake integration utilizes ADBC (Arrow Database Connectivity) for optimal efficiency and seamless integration with Explorer. Connecting to Microsoft SQL Server is also straightforward.

recent_posts.title: Introducing File Integration
recent_posts.summary: Livebook v0.11 introduces file integration, allowing users to add files to their notebooks, generate code suggestions based on the file type, and perform lazy data reading and manipulation. Files in Livebook can be references or attachments, and users can work with large datasets without requiring substantial memory.

recent_posts.title: Speech-to-text with Whisper: timestamping, streaming, and parallelism, oh-my!
recent_posts.summary: The Whisper speech-to-text model now includes timestamping, streaming capabilities, and parallelism, allowing for faster transcriptions of larger audio files. Elixir developers can now easily transcribe audio using the integrated Neural Network Task in Livebook. Download the latest version and give it a try!

recent_posts.title: Remote execution Smart cell
recent_posts.summary: Livebook introduces a new Smart cell called Remote execution, which allows for calling code from other nodes. It eliminates the limitations of the 'Attached node' runtime and provides features such as autocompletion and docs preview for modules defined in the remote node.

recent_posts.title: Livebook is sponsoring SpawnFest again
recent_posts.summary: Livebook is sponsoring Spawnfest again - Livebook.dev. Spawnfest is an annual 48-hour online software development contest in which teams worldwide get one weekend to create the best BEAM-based applications they can. Livebook Apps is a feature we launched earlier this year that enables you to turn your notebook into an interactive web application.

top_posts.title: Build and deploy a Whisper chat app to Hugging Face in 15 minutes
top_posts.summary: Learn how to build and deploy a Whisper chat app to Hugging Face using Livebook. The app allows users to communicate through audio messages converted to text using the Whisper Machine Learning model. Explore the cool features of Livebook, such as deploying notebooks as apps, real-time and multiplayer functionality, and concurrent machine learning. Get the latest version of Livebook to run the Whisper chat app yourself.
